functional_semantics.triton: Q1*cos - Q2*sin into the first half and Q2*cos + Q1*sin into the second half of each head, tables indexed by row % seqlen (impl_triton.py 29-32, 47-48).
functional_semantics.cutile: q1*cos - q2*sin and q2*cos + q1*sin on the (B*S, H, 2, D/2) view, tables indexed by row_id % SeqLen (impl_cutile.py 33-39, 49-53, 68).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise impl_torch.py 11-21 (half-split pairing, position-only table indexing); rotate_half (3-6) is dead code in the reference; BACKWARD_PASS is constant False on the Triton side (83, 96).

stages.triton: clone of q into output (68) then one in-place rotation kernel, grid (B*S, ceil(H/group)) (75, 88-89).
stages.cutile: clone of q into output (63) then one in-place rotation kernel, grid (B*S, ceil(H/group), 1) (98-102).
stages.note: Identical clone-then-in-place structure; the contract permits out-of-place as an equivalent mapping since the clone is pure data movement.

dependencies.triton: Kernel depends only on the clone; every (row, head, pair) handled by exactly one program (37-48).
dependencies.cutile: Kernel depends only on the clone; every (row, head, pair) handled by exactly one CTA (42-53).
dependencies.note: Elementwise; no cross-program dependency on either side.

precision.triton: Q1/Q2 cast to sin1.dtype (= input dtype) and multiplied natively; no fp32 upcast (44-48).
precision.cutile: Loads and arithmetic in the tensor dtype; no ct.astype in the kernel (42-50).
precision.note: Both compute in the input dtype like the reference; config verify atol/rtol 5e-3 (config.yaml 1-3) covers fp16.

preprocessing.triton: output = q.clone().contiguous() inside run() (68); BLOCK derived from head_dim (71); strides passed (77-79).
preprocessing.cutile: output = q.clone().contiguous() inside run() (63); 4-D views of output/cos/sin (68-70); autotune path clones a second scratch tmp per call (77).
preprocessing.note: Both pay a full timed copy of q before the kernel; the extra tmp clone on the cuTile autotune path is tuner-only and does not affect the default-path boundary.

intermediate_storage.triton: None beyond the output clone, which is the kernel's in/out buffer (68).
intermediate_storage.cutile: None beyond the output clone (63); tmp (77) exists only on the autotune path.
intermediate_storage.note: No global scratch on either side.

mutation.triton: q, cos, sin untouched; the fresh clone is rotated in place (47-48); restore_value=['Q'] protects tuning trials (61).
mutation.cutile: q, cos, sin untouched; the fresh clone is rotated in place (52-53); tuning targets tmp (89).
mutation.note: Idempotent on both sides; the contract forbids input mutation and requires a non-aliasing output.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: bytes_expr counts one read of q and one write of the output (config.yaml 24). Both timed run() bodies first clone q (read + write of the whole tensor, impl_triton.py 68 / impl_cutile.py 63) and then read and write the clone in the kernel, so the measured region moves about twice the counted bytes; the (S, D/2) table reads are also uncounted. The formula matches an out-of-place implementation, which the contract permits. flops_expr (3 per element) matches the arithmetic.

review_items: Both references clone q inside the timed run() and rotate the clone in place, moving ~2x the bytes_expr model; the contract requires a non-aliasing fresh output but permits an out-of-place mapping that meets the 2n model. Decide whether bytes_expr stays as the minimal 2n bound (generated out-of-place kernels may then outperform the references for non-algorithmic reasons) or whether the references should be re-measured out-of-place. Non-blocking for the contract text.
